question: In December 2023, who became the first women Chief of Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nina Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In December 2023, IPS officer Nina Singh became the first woman Director General (Chief) of the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF). (नीना सिंह — CISF की पहली महिला महानिदेशक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The CISF is a Central Armed Police Force (CAPF) under the Ministry of Home Affairs, raised in 1969. It guards airports, metros, nuclear and space installations, ports and other vital establishments.

• Nina Singh is a 1989-batch IPS officer of the Rajasthan cadre.

NOTE

• Archana Ramasundaram was the first woman DG of a paramilitary force (SSB) in 2016. The CISF's motto is "Protection and Security".

question: The autobiography, 'An Autobiography' by Jawaharlal Nehru is also known as ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Toward Freedom.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jawaharlal Nehru's work "An Autobiography" (1936) is also known as "Toward Freedom". He wrote it largely during his imprisonment in 1934–35. (नेहरू की आत्मकथा — Toward Freedom)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other famous works by Nehru: "The Discovery of India", "Glimpses of World History" and "Letters from a Father to His Daughter".

• Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first Prime Minister (1947–1964); his birthday, 14 November, is celebrated as Children's Day.

NOTE

• "The Accidental Prime Minister" was written by Sanjaya Baru (on Manmohan Singh). "The Unfinished Innings" is not associated with Nehru.

question: In which of the following states is the groundnut fair, 'Kadalekayi Parishe' celebrated on the last Monday of the Karthika month of the Hindu calendar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kadalekayi Parishe" (the groundnut fair) is a traditional fair celebrated in Bengaluru, Karnataka, on the last Monday of the Karthika month. Farmers offer the first crop of groundnuts to Lord Basavanna (the Nandi bull). (कदलेकायी परिशे — कर्नाटक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The fair is held around the Bull Temple (Dodda Basavana Gudi) in Basavanagudi, Bengaluru.

• "Kadalekayi" means groundnut/peanut in Kannada; "Parishe" means fair.

NOTE

• Other fairs of India: Pushkar Fair (Rajasthan), Sonepur Cattle Fair (Bihar), Hemis Festival (Ladakh).

question: The earthquakes that are generated due to the explosion of chemical or nuclear devices are known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Explosion earthquakes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Explosion earthquakes" are the earthquakes caused by the detonation of chemical or nuclear devices. The ground shakes due to the energy released by the explosion. (विस्फोट भूकंप)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Tectonic earthquakes — caused by the movement of tectonic plates (the most common type).

• Volcanic earthquakes — associated with volcanic activity.

• Collapse earthquakes — caused by the collapse of underground caverns/mines.

• Reservoir-induced earthquakes — caused by the pressure of water in large dams/reservoirs.

NOTE

• Earthquakes are measured by the Richter scale (magnitude) and their intensity by the Mercalli scale. The instrument used is the seismograph.

question: Which of the following gases is generally used to flush bags of chips by the manufacturers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitrogen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Nitrogen" gas is used to flush (fill) bags of chips. Being an inert (non-reactive) gas, it prevents the chips from being oxidised (going rancid), keeps them crisp, and cushions them against breakage. (नाइट्रोजन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Nitrogen (N₂) makes up about 78% of the Earth's atmosphere and is chemically inert at normal temperatures.

• Oxygen would spoil the food by oxidation, so it is deliberately removed.

NOTE

• Uses of nitrogen: food packaging, making ammonia (Haber process), liquid nitrogen for freezing, and filling tyres. Its symbol is N, atomic number 7.

question: In the year 1940, the national games were hosted by which of the following cities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the year 1940, the National Games of India were hosted by the city of Bombay (now Mumbai). (1940 के राष्ट्रीय खेल — बंबई/मुंबई)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The National Games of India are a multi-sport event featuring athletes from different states and union territories.

• The Games were first held (as the Indian Olympic Games) in 1924 at Lahore.

NOTE

• Recent editions: the 36th National Games were held in Gujarat (2022) and the 37th in Goa (2023).

question: Who among the following was the founder of 'Satnami movement' in the central India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghasidas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Ghasidas founded the "Satnami movement" in central India (the Chhattisgarh region) in the early 19th century. He preached the worship of one formless God ("Satnam" — the true name) and opposed caste discrimination and untouchability. (गुरु घासीदास — सतनामी आंदोलन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Guru Ghasidas worked among the Chamar community, promoting equality, truth and rejection of idol worship and rituals.

• The Guru Ghasidas National Park in Chhattisgarh is named after him.

NOTE

• There was also an earlier Satnami sect founded by Birbhan in the 17th century (Narnaul region), which revolted against Aurangzeb in 1672.

question: What does a budget deficit indicate?
option_1: The government is saving for future projects
option_2: The government is not allocating enough funds for public services
solution_text:
The correct answer is Government spending exceeds government revenue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "budget deficit" occurs when the government's total expenditure (spending) exceeds its total revenue (income) in a given period. (बजट घाटा — व्यय > राजस्व)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• When revenue exceeds spending, it is a budget surplus; when they are equal, it is a balanced budget.

• Governments often finance a deficit through borrowing (loans, bonds).

NOTE

• Related terms: Fiscal Deficit (total expenditure – total revenue excluding borrowings), Revenue Deficit, and Primary Deficit (fiscal deficit – interest payments).

question: In which of the following years was the state of Golconda finally annexed into the Mughal empire?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1687.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Golconda Sultanate (ruled by the Qutb Shahi dynasty) was finally annexed into the Mughal Empire in 1687 by Emperor Aurangzeb. (गोलकुंडा का मुगल साम्राज्य में विलय — 1687)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Aurangzeb had annexed the Bijapur Sultanate (Adil Shahi dynasty) in 1686, just a year earlier.

• Golconda (near Hyderabad) was famous for its diamonds (including the Kohinoor) and its strong fort.

NOTE

• The Deccan Sultanates were: Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar, Bidar and Berar, formed after the break-up of the Bahmani Kingdom.

question: Palkigundu Minor Rock Edicts of Ashoka are located in _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Palkigundu (Pakligundu) Minor Rock Edicts" of the Mauryan emperor Ashoka are located in the Koppal district of Karnataka. (अशोक के पलकीगुंडु लघु शिलालेख — कर्नाटक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Many of Ashoka's Minor Rock Edicts are found in Karnataka (e.g., at Maski, Brahmagiri, Gavimath, Palkigundu, Siddapura, Jatinga-Rameshwara).

• The Maski and Gujarra edicts are important because they mention Ashoka by his personal name "Ashoka (Devanampiya Asoka)".

NOTE

• Ashoka's edicts were mostly written in the Brahmi script and Prakrit language. They were first deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837.

question: The Great Granary was one of the largest granaries in the _______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harappan Civilization.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Great Granary" was one of the largest structures of the Harappan (Indus Valley) Civilization, found at Mohenjo-daro (and a similar granary at Harappa). It was used to store surplus grain. (हड़प्पा सभ्यता — विशाल अन्नागार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Great Bath (a large public water tank) was also found at Mohenjo-daro.

• The Harappan Civilization (c. 2500 BCE) flourished along the Indus and Ghaggar-Hakra rivers and is known for town planning, drainage and standardised bricks.

NOTE

• Important Harappan sites: Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira, Lothal (dockyard), Kalibangan (ploughed field), Rakhigarhi.

question: Who among the following Indian dancers was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan in 1971, who was also known as the father of modern Indian dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uday Shankar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Uday Shankar, honoured with the Padma Vibhushan in 1971, is regarded as the "father of modern Indian dance". He created a unique style blending classical Indian dance with European techniques. (उदय शंकर — आधुनिक भारतीय नृत्य के जनक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Uday Shankar was the elder brother of the sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar.

• His famous film "Kalpana (1948)" showcased his innovative dance style.

NOTE

• Pandit Birju Maharaj was a legend of Kathak; Kelucharan Mohapatra was a maestro of Odissi; Pandit Durga Lal was a noted Kathak dancer.

question: As on February 2024, Nitish Kumar is the 9th time Chief Minister of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As on February 2024, Nitish Kumar took oath as the Chief Minister of Bihar for the 9th time. (नीतीश कुमार — बिहार के मुख्यमंत्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Nitish Kumar is the leader of the Janata Dal (United) [JD(U)] party.

• Bihar's capital is Patna; its Governor (as of that period) and the CM head the state executive.

NOTE

• The Chief Minister is the real executive head of a state, appointed by the Governor under Article 164 of the Constitution.

question: In the 1974 edition of the Guinness Book of Records, which playback singer was mentioned as the most recorded artist in human history?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lata Mangeshkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the 1974 edition of the Guinness Book of Records, the legendary playback singer Lata Mangeshkar was mentioned as the most recorded artist in human history. (लता मंगेशकर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Lata Mangeshkar (the "Nightingale of India") received the Bharat Ratna (2001), the Dadasaheb Phalke Award and numerous other honours.

• She sang in many Indian languages over a career spanning several decades.

NOTE

• P. Susheela and K. S. Chithra are celebrated South Indian playback singers, also recognised by Guinness for a large number of recorded songs.

question: What is the female literacy rate in India, as per the 2011 census?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 65.46%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of 2011, the female literacy rate in India was 65.46%. (2011 जनगणना — महिला साक्षरता दर 65.46%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The overall literacy rate in 2011 was 74.04%, with male literacy at 82.14% and female at 65.46%.

• Kerala had the highest literacy rate; Bihar the lowest.

NOTE

• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census; its slogan was "Our Census, Our Future". Literacy is defined as the ability to read and write with understanding in any language, for those aged 7 and above.

question: Forward Bloc was founded in 1939-40 by which of the following leaders?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Subhash Chandra Bose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "All India Forward Bloc" was founded by Subhas Chandra Bose in 1939 (formally in 1940), after he resigned as the President of the Indian National Congress. (फॉरवर्ड ब्लॉक — सुभाष चंद्र बोस)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Subhas Chandra Bose had won the Congress Presidency at Tripuri (1939) defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya, but resigned due to differences with Gandhiji.

• He later organised the Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army) and gave the slogan "Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom".

NOTE

• Rash Behari Bose helped establish the INA/Indian Independence League in East Asia. Bose is fondly called "Netaji"; 23 January (his birthday) is observed as Parakram Diwas.

question: Dandiya Raas is a famous dance form of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dandiya Raas" is a famous folk dance of the state of Gujarat, performed with decorated sticks (dandiyas), especially during the festival of Navratri. (डांडिया रास — गुजरात)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Garba" is another popular folk dance of Gujarat associated with Navratri; in 2023, Garba was inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list.

• Dandiya Raas symbolises a playful, mock-fight dance associated with Goddess Durga and Lord Krishna.

NOTE

• Folk dances: Bhangra/Giddha (Punjab), Ghoomar (Rajasthan), Bihu (Assam), Garba/Dandiya (Gujarat), Lavani (Maharashtra).

question: Which of the following is/are the highest judiciary in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Supreme Court.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Supreme Court of India" is the highest judicial body (apex court) in India. It is the final court of appeal and the guardian of the Constitution. (सर्वोच्च न्यायालय — भारत की सर्वोच्च न्यायपालिका)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Supreme Court was established on 28 January 1950 and is located in New Delhi.

• The judicial hierarchy is: Supreme Court → High Courts → District/Subordinate Courts.

NOTE

• Articles 124–147 deal with the Supreme Court. The Chief Justice of India (CJI) heads it. Judges are appointed by the President and retire at the age of 65.

question: The Mayurbhanj District in Odisha is a part of which Biosphere Reserve from the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Similipal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mayurbhanj district of Odisha is home to the "Similipal Biosphere Reserve", which includes the Similipal Tiger Reserve and National Park. (सिमिलिपाल बायोस्फीयर रिज़र्व — मयूरभंज, ओडिशा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Similipal is famous for its melanistic (black) tigers, elephants, waterfalls (Barehipani, Joranda) and rich sal forests.

• It was designated a Biosphere Reserve in 1994 and is part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves (2009).

NOTE

• Other biosphere reserves: Dehang-Debang (Arunachal Pradesh), Pachmarhi (Madhya Pradesh), Nokrek (Meghalaya), Nilgiri (India's first, 1986).

question: As per Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, what is the total length of National Highways in India as of November 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1,44,634 kilometres.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH), the total length of National Highways in India as of November 2022 was about 1,44,634 kilometres. (राष्ट्रीय राजमार्गों की लंबाई)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• National Highways form only a small share of the total road network but carry a large share of the traffic.

• India has one of the largest road networks in the world; road transport is managed by MoRTH and the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).

NOTE

• The NHAI was set up in 1988. NH 44 (Srinagar to Kanyakumari) is the longest National Highway in India.

question: Which of the following neighbouring countries of India is most populous?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pakistan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given neighbouring countries of India, "Pakistan" is the most populous (with a population of over 24 crore/240 million), higher than Bangladesh, Afghanistan and Bhutan. (पाकिस्तान — सर्वाधिक जनसंख्या)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India shares land borders with Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Afghanistan.

• Bangladesh (~17 crore) is the next most populous among the options, followed by Afghanistan and then Bhutan (least populous).

NOTE

• India's longest land border is with Bangladesh (~4,096 km); the border with Pakistan is guarded by the Border Security Force (BSF).

question: Who among the following athletes was conferred with the Arjuna Award, 2021 by President Ram Nath Kovind?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arpinder Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Arpinder Singh, the Indian triple jump athlete, was conferred with the Arjuna Award in 2021 by President Ram Nath Kovind. (अर्पिंदर सिंह — अर्जुन पुरस्कार 2021)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Arpinder Singh won the gold medal in triple jump at the 2018 Asian Games (Jakarta).

• The Arjuna Award is given for outstanding performance in sports over a period of years (usually four years).

NOTE

• India's top sports honours: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna (highest), Arjuna Award, Dronacharya Award (coaches), Dhyan Chand Award (lifetime achievement).

question: Which of the following is the federal feature of the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bicameralism.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bicameralism" (a two-house Parliament — the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, the latter representing the states) is a federal feature of the Indian Constitution. (द्विसदनीयता — संघीय विशेषता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Federal features: written Constitution, division of powers (Union, State and Concurrent lists), supremacy of the Constitution, independent judiciary and bicameralism.

• Unitary features: single citizenship, integrated judiciary, All-India Services, strong Centre and emergency provisions.

NOTE

• The Indian Constitution is described as "federal in form but unitary in spirit" (a quasi-federal Constitution). The term "Federation" is not used; Article 1 calls India a "Union of States".

question: When a sailor jumps out of a rowing boat, the boat moves backwards. This represents:
solution_text:
The correct answer is the First law of motion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Per the given official key, when a sailor jumps out of a rowing boat and the boat moves backwards, it is treated as an illustration of the First law of motion (law of inertia) — the action of the sailor changes the state of the boat's rest. (न्यूटन का पहला गति नियम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia): a body continues in its state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.

• Newton's Second Law: Force = mass × acceleration (F = ma).

• Newton's Third Law: to every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

NOTE

• The recoil of a boat/gun and the motion of a rocket are classic examples used to illustrate Newton's laws of motion; conceptually the boat's backward motion also relates to conservation of momentum.

question: When the body is deprived of energy from food, which of the following tissues is used to feed on its own?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Adipose tissue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Adipose tissue" (a type of connective tissue that stores fat) is used by the body as a reserve energy source when it is deprived of energy from food. Stored fat is broken down to release energy during starvation. (वसा ऊतक — ऊर्जा भंडार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Adipose tissue is found beneath the skin and around internal organs; it also insulates the body and cushions organs.

• Nervous tissue transmits impulses; epithelial tissue covers/lines body surfaces; collenchyma is a plant tissue (not animal).

NOTE

• The four main animal tissue types are epithelial, connective (including adipose, blood, bone), muscular and nervous tissues.
